page.layout: One page of running text in a single column; marginal notes in the right margin beside the second paragraph (a section number "2." and the authority "Prosper Aquitanicus"); signature "A 5" at the foot; printed page number "8" at the head.

main_text.p: est, quàm prædestinare ad malum; vel, ut Scriptura loquitur, Prov.16.v.4. crea- » re etiam impium ad diem malum? Quid » aliud, quod de Pharaone: Ad hoc te exci- » tavi, ut ostenda in te potentiam meam? Rom. 9.v.17.ex Exod.9.v.15. Est ne malum, fi- gulum facere vas in ignominiam? Rom. » 9.v.21,22. Hoc malum foret, punire id quod jusseris. Eo nomine, aliisq; multis, ut videre est apud Profperum, tunc Galli calumniabantur doctrinam Augustini. Quare Concilij verba non sunt asseverativa; sed hypothetica: si qui sunt.

Eodem sensu dicit Prosper, primo 2. Sententiâ 14. ad objecta capitula Gallo-Prosper Aquitanicus rum: Qui dicit, quòd, qui Evangelicæ prædicationi non credunt; ex Dei prædestinatione non credunt, (quasi ex præcepto; & non propriâ malitiâ, voluntate. Intelligitur id ex sequentibus verbis) & quòd Deus ita definiverit, ut, quicunque non credunt, ex ipsius constitutione (h. e. præcepto aut mandato) non credant: non est Catholicus.
Clarius adhuc, in sequentibus in eâ-

page.notes: Top of the page carries a small printed mark above the first line ("8." with ornament); read as the page number 8, with some doubt. The "»" marks at line ends after "crea-", "Quid", "exci-", "Rom." and "Rom." are small printed signs; copied as they appear, but uncertain. The marginal label beside the second paragraph reads "Prosper Aquitanicus" (the second line is partly worn: "quitanicus"), so the spelling is doubtful. The first word "est" and the italic "sunt." at the end of the first paragraph have long-s forms; written with plain s. Faint show-through of the neighbouring page along the left edge is not transcribed.
